one_liner: A 7-year-old male with a retained wooden foreign body in the right foot following a bike accident underwent successful incision, drainage, and foreign body removal.

key_findings.name: periwound erythema
key_findings.interpretation: remaining periwound erythema noted on exam

key_findings.name: mild crepitation
key_findings.interpretation: mild crepitation about 2 cm proximal from the entry wound

key_findings.name: wound probing to bone
key_findings.interpretation: area along third metatarsal head that did probe to the bone

procedures.name: Removal of foreign body, right foot
procedures.outcome: large wooden foreign body and small pieces removed

course.narrative: A 7-year-old male inpatient with a history of falling off his bike and a retained wooden root foreign body in his right foot, complicated by ongoing purulent drainage despite previous I&D, was brought to the operating room under general anesthesia. Examination revealed periwound erythema, mild crepitation, and an entry wound over the third metatarsal head. The wound was extended, and a large wooden foreign body along with several small pieces were successfully removed. The wound probed to the bone distally, but no purulent drainage was expressed. The area was thoroughly flushed, pulse lavaged with 3 liters of plain sterile saline, and wound cultures (aerobic and aerobic) were obtained. The wound was packed with sterile new gauze and dressed. The patient tolerated the procedure well, was transported to the PACU with stable vitals, and was returned to pediatrics for ongoing podiatry care.

disposition.condition: vital signs stable and vascular status intact
